name: One-leg stand
rangeNote: A fitness test, so there is no lab range: your result is compared with people of your age and sex in published norm tables (shown on this page).
summary: How many seconds you can stand on one leg without support. It reflects standing balance, which relies on the legs, the inner ear, sight and the nerves that sense where your feet are. It can be done with eyes open, and as a harder version with eyes closed.

high.meaning: Standing longer on one leg for your age means better balance.

low.meaning: Not managing 10 seconds on one leg at ages 51–75 was linked to higher death rates in one study. Poor balance can have many causes; a doctor can look into it, especially after a fall.
